subject: Helios dedicated headroom commitment — finance & ops handoff
messages:
From: Ashley Greene <ashley@helios.health>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helios.health
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool request & headroom ask for Q3 pilot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profiles looked great. We ran the internal traffic forecast and believe we will need a small dedicated slice for our Q3 pilot (estimated 6–8 gpus equivalent sustained, with two 2-hour daily burst windows for end-of-day reporting).

Can Redwood provide: 
- A short-term reserved commitment (3 months) with an option to renew monthly thereafter
- A proposed autoscale exception for the two daily 2-hour bursts (we can tolerate slightly higher latency during those windows)
- A cost estimate that includes unit pricing and an emergency burst fee schedule

I've attached our forecast workbook (helios-forecast.xlsx) — the traffic tab is the useful slice. Please loop in whoever owns capacity & finance so we can get a quote and agree on SLA/eviction tolerances.

Looking forward — ideally we can lock something by end of next week to align procurement cycles.

Best,
Ashley Greene
Director of Platform Engineering
Helios Health

Attachment: helios-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ashley Greene <ashley@helios.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool request & headroom ask for Q3 pilot

Ashley — thanks for the workbook and the clear ask. Looping in Marissa (sales) and Jonas (capacity/product) to confirm feasibility and provide a quote.

Marissa / Jonas: high level ask from Helios: 3-month reserved commitment (6–8 gpus equivalent sustained) + temporary autoscale exception for 2x 2-hour burst windows/day. They want a cost schedule and explicit burst pricing. Workbook attached by customer; see traffic tab.

Immediate asks: 
- Jonas: can we support a targeted reserve that size in us-west region for a 3-month window starting 2026-07-01? If not, propose alternatives (e.g., smaller slice + burst lane).
- Marissa: I need a procurement path and any standard commercial levers (upfront discount, early-renew option) we usually offer for short pilots.
- I will coordinate Ops/Finance handoff and confirm SLA/eviction tolerances.

Ashley: we'll come back with a proposed mutual action plan & quote. If you have a signed MSA or preferred terms, send them over.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Product — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ashley Greene <ashley@helios.health>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool request & headroom ask for Q3 pilot

Kimberly / Marissa — quick technical read.

Summary: feasible but requires an autoscale policy exception and a small config change to the burst lane. Ops notes: 
- Sustained 6–8 GPU-equivalent: we can provision a 6-GPU reserved slab with soft-burst headroom up to 10 GPUs for short windows, provided Helios accepts a higher token-cost multiplier during burst (we should price as "burst units").
- The two 2-hour windows daily are predictable — we can set a scheduled policy which prioritizes their slab for those windows and relaxes strict adherence outside them.
- Eviction tolerance: recommend we set preemption threshold to 20% (i.e., low-priority preemption) and provide a 15-minute warmup notice for larger evictions.

Constraints / ops concerns: 
- If we grant burst headroom, we should limit burst frequency (max 2 windows/day) and require they provide a daily schedule in advance (cron-style).
- This will require a temporary autoscale exception record and an ops-runbook for handling overflow.

I'll draft a short ops runbook and a config snippet.

Jonas
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Quote: "schedule a short sync with Ops to confirm runbook and SLA wording."

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Thanks team — procurement checklist from Finance/Legal perspective below.

Procurement steps we need to complete before committing capacity: 
1) Confirm commitment term and bill cadence (Helios asked for 3 months, please confirm start date).
2) Confirm deal ID and PO approach (we'll need either a signed PO or DocuSign signature on a short SOW).
3) Finalize pricing and any pilot discounts — Marissa to propose pricing bands and discount rationale.
4) Attachment of the schedule (autoscale exception) into the SOW as Exhibit A (Jonas will provide config/runbook).
5) Security/compliance checklist: Helios must confirm any special network/KMS requirements for private deployments (if applicable).

I've attached a draft reserved quote (reserved-quote-v1.pdf) with line items for base reserved slab and burst multipliers. Marissa — flag any commercial edits.

If we can get signed SOW/PO by 2026-05-25 we should be able to lock capacity for a 2026-07-01 start.

David Kim
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: reserved-quote-v1.pdf (PDF)
